newsitem.title: UK: Britain accuses Sinn Fein of hypocrisy.
newsitem.headline: Britain accuses Sinn Fein of hypocrisy.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major's office has written to Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams telling him it is "hypocritical" to talk of peace following last week's killing of a British soldier in Northern Ireland.
An aide to Major said on Tuesday the letter, sent in the last day or two, turned down Adams' request for a meeting between Sinn Fein and British government officials.

Later Martin McGuinness, a senior colleague of Adams, accused Britain of inflexibility. Major's refusal came "as a disappointment to those who are genuinely interested in rebuilding the peace process," McGuinness, who is on the executive of Sinn Fein, said in a statement issued in Belfast.
Sinn Fein is the political wing of the Irish Republican Army which is suspected of being responsible for the shooting dead of soldier Stephen Restorick at an army checkpoint on Wednesday.
"We have told Mr Adams it is hypocritical to talk about peace when people are being killed," the aide said.
He added that the letter had reiterated Britain's long-standing position towards Sinn Fein.

Major has repeatedly made it clear that the organisation cannot be allowed into all-party talks on the future of Northern Ireland until it renews the 17-month ceasefire which it ended a year ago, and satisfies Britain that this time the truce was permanent.

Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Patrick Mayhew said on Saturday that it was "certainly not appropriate" for British officials to meet Sinn Fein following Restorick's killing and other violent incidents.
The IRA wants the unification of the island of Ireland and the end of British rule in Northern Ireland.
